Banal

/buh-NAL/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Banal means dull, commonplace, and lacking originality.

Banal means dull, commonplace, and lacking originality. The critic dismissed the summer blockbuster as banal, complaining that its plot recycled the same tired rescue mission audiences had already seen a dozen times.

Worked Example

As a judge for the town's annual slogan contest, Mr. Okafor read hundreds of entries, and by lunchtime they had blurred into one banal stream of 'Shop local!' and 'A town with heart.' Only a single entry, a slogan written as a riddle, felt genuinely fresh.

The recycled, interchangeable slogans show no originality at all, which is exactly what makes them banal.

How Banal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

trite

trite: worn out and stale from constant overuse

humdrum

humdrum: boringly ordinary and routine

hackneyed

hackneyed: made dull by endless repetition

Antonyms

fresh

fresh: new and interesting

original

original: created firsthand rather than copied

How Strong Is It? — ordinary → banal → vapid

ordinary vs. banal

ordinary vs. banal: Something ordinary is simply common without being a flaw, while something banal is so unoriginal that it bores its audience.

vapid vs. banal

vapid vs. banal: A banal remark is dull and overfamiliar, but a vapid one is completely empty of thought or meaning.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — ban

Root — ban: from an old Germanic word for a ruler's official proclamation binding the whole community

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: adjective-forming ending

Put it together

Put it together: Banal began as a feudal legal term: the ban was a lord's proclamation, and things called banal, like the village mill and oven, belonged to everyone in the community under that decree. Because they were shared by all, banal drifted from 'common to all' into 'commonplace,' and finally into 'so commonplace it is dull.'

Use the root in a new word: abandon

Use the root in a new word: abandon: When the knight chose to abandon his post, he placed himself 'at the ban,' under someone else's control, the same old proclamation root that later gave us banal.

Word Choice

neutral, mildly critical

Banal is a criticism of originality, not of craftsmanship: a banal movie can be slickly produced and still say nothing new. It is most often applied to remarks, plots, slogans, and ideas rather than to physical objects.
